# Connecticut'ta Düğün Sigortası – Sorumluluk ve İptal Teminatına İhtiyacınız Var mı?
Source: https://aia-danbury.com/blog/tr/wedding-insurance-need

Yazar: Ron T. Boucher • Güncelleme: 19 Ekim 2026

Connecticut'ta bir düğün planlamak — ister Danbury yakınlarındaki Candlewood Gölü kıyısında bir malikanede, ister Bridgeport'ta tarihi bir sahil mekanında veya Litchfield County'de bir bağ evinde olsun — hem unutulmaz bir kutlamayı hem de önemli bir finansal yatırımı temsil eder. The Knot 2025 Real Weddings Study raporuna (study report) göre, Connecticut ve çevresinde ortalama bir düğün $36,000 ila $48,000 arasında mal olmakta ve çiftler aylar öncesinden $15,000 ila $25,000 tutarında iade edilmeyen tedarikçi depozitosu ödemektedir.

Büyük gününüzde beklenmedik bir kasırga, tedarikçi iflası veya konuk yaralanması meydana gelirse, şansa veya standart ev sigortası poliçenize güvenmek sizi beş haneli mali kayıplarla karşı karşıya bırakabilir.

Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I) tarafından yayınlanan 2025 özel etkinlik sigortalama raporuna (report) göre, Connecticut'taki her nişanlı çiftin üç temel sigorta tanımını anlaması şarttır:

- **Özel etkinlik sorumluluk sigortası,** 2025 Insurance Information Institute raporuna (report) göre prova yemeği, tören ve resepsiyon sırasında üçüncü şahıs bedensel yaralanmaları ve mekan mülk hasarları için $1,000,000 ila $2,000,000 teminat sağlayan kısa vadeli bir genel sorumluluk sözleşmesidir.
- **Ev sahibi alkol sorumluluğu teminatı,** resepsiyonda alkol ikram edilen bir konuğun mekandan ayrıldıktan sonra trafik kazasına veya yaralanmaya yol açması durumunda düğün sahiplerini savunan ve tazmin eden özel bir yasal korumadır.
- **Düğün iptal ve erteleme teminatı,** şiddetli hava koşulları, ani hastalık veya tedarikçi iflası nedeniyle tarihin yeniden planlanması gerektiğinde kaybedilen iade edilmeyen depozitoları kurtaran bir finansal geri ödeme poliçesidir.

---

## Connecticut'ta İki Ana Düğün Sigortası Teminat Türü Nelerdir?

Düğün sigortası, mekanların Sigorta Sertifikası şartlarını karşılayan ve konuk yaralanmalarını veya alkol kazalarını kapsayan Üçüncü Şahıs Özel Etkinlik Sorumluluğu ile beklenmedik acil durumlar nedeniyle kaybedilen iade edilmeyen depozitoları geri ödeyen İptal veya Erteleme Teminatından oluşan ikili bir koruma planıdır.

Her iki bölümün nasıl çalıştığını anlamak, birikimlerinizi korurken mekanınızın yasal sözleşme şartlarını eksiksiz karşılamanızı sağlar.

### İptal veya Erteleme Teminatı İade Edilmeyen Depozitoları Nasıl Korur?

Düğün iptal teminatı, şiddetli bir kasırga, ani hastaneye yatış veya tedarikçi iflası gibi sigortalı bir tehlikenin töreni veya resepsiyonu ertelemeye zorlaması durumunda çiftlere iade edilmeyen mekan, yemek, çiçek ve fotoğrafçılık depozitolarını geri ödeyen bir finansal tazminat korumasıdır.

Travelers Insurance tarafından yayınlanan 2025 düğün hasar analiz raporuna (study report) göre, tedarikçi sorunları ve şiddetli hava koşulları tüm düğün erteleme taleplerinin %62'sinden fazlasını oluşturmaktadır:

- **Şiddetli Hava Koşulları:** Yolları kapatan, mekanın elektriğini kesen veya çiftin, kilit aile üyelerinin ya da konukların çoğunun mekana ulaşmasını engelleyen büyük bir fırtına, kasırga veya tipi.
- **Ani Hastalık, Yaralanma veya Askeri Görev:** Gelin, damat veya birinci derece aile üyelerinin beklenmedik şekilde hastaneye kaldırılması ya da askeri iznin aniden iptal edilmesi.
- **Tedarikçi İflası veya Gelmemesi:** Bir düğün salonunun, yemek şirketinin, çiçekçinin veya fotoğrafçının iflas etmesi ya da törene gelmemesi durumunda hem kaybedilen depozitonuzu hem de son dakika alternatif maliyet farkını karşılar.
- **Özel Kıyafet, Yüzük ve Hediyeler:** İsteğe bağlı alt limitler hasar gören gelinlikleri, kaybolan alyansları, bozulan düğün pastalarını ve resepsiyonda çalınan hediyeleri kapsar.

### Connecticut Düğün Mekanları Neden Özel Etkinlik ve Alkol Sorumluluğu Şart Koşar?

Özel etkinlik ve ev sahibi alkol sorumluluğu, 2025 mekan araştırması raporuna (survey report) göre Connecticut'taki davet salonları ve bağ evleri tarafından zorunlu tutulan, $1,000,000 birincil mekan sorumluluğu ve alkol savunması sağlayarak mülk sahibini Ek Sigortalı gösteren bir poliçedir.

2025 Connecticut Insurance Department (CID) tüketici raporuna (report) ve Connecticut Genel Yasaları Bölüm 30-102'ye (Dram Shop Act) göre, alkol sunan işletmeler ve ev sahipleri, aşırı alkol alan bir konuğun resepsiyondan ayrıldıktan sonra trafik kazasına neden olması halinde yaralanan kişi başına $250,000+ yasal sorumlulukla karşı karşıya kalır. Bu nedenle seçkin Connecticut mekanları, düğünden 30 gün önce olay başına $1,000,000 / toplamda $2,000,000 limitli ve sıfır muafiyetli bir Sigorta Sertifikası (COI) sunulmasını şart koşar.

| Teminat Boyutu | Düğün İptali ve Erteleme | Özel Etkinlik ve Alkol Sorumluluğu | Standart CT Ev Poliçesi (HO-3) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Temel Koruma Amacı** | İade edilmeyen tedarikçi depozitolarını geri öder | Mekan mülk hasarını ve konuk yaralanmalarını öder | Konutunuzu korur; ev dışı sorumluluk sınırlıdır |
| **Tipik Poliçe Maliyeti** | $225 – $650 ($15,000 – $75,000 bütçeye göre) | $1,000,000 / $2,000,000 limit için $150 – $275 | Ev primine dahildir ancak ticari mekanları hariç tutar |
| **Mekan COI ve Ek Sigortalı** | Mekanın sorumluluk COI şartını karşılamaz | Mekanı Ek Sigortalı gösteren resmi COI düzenler | Ticari mekanları neredeyse hiçbir zaman Ek Sigortalı yapmaz |
| **Ev Sahibi Alkol Sorumluluğu** | Dahil değildir | Dahildir veya $50 karşılığında eklenir (açık barı kapsar) | Çok sınırlıdır; kiralık barmenleri veya salonları hariç tutar |
| **Tedarikçi İflası / Gelmemesi** | Poliçe limitine kadar karşılanır (depozitoları öder) | Karşılanmaz | $0 teminat |
| **Tipik Muafiyet** | İptal talebi başına $0 – $250 | $0 – $1,000 mülk hasarı muafiyeti | $1,000 – $2,500 mülk muafiyeti |
*Kaynak (source): Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I) ve Connecticut Insurance Department (CID) tarafından yayınlanan 2025 özel etkinlik sigortalama raporu (report) verilerine göre.*

---

## Standart Bir Düğün Sigortası Poliçesinde Neler Hariç Tutulur?

Düğün sigortası istisnaları, gelin veya damadın kendi isteğiyle fikir değiştirmesini, poliçe kesilmeden önce bilinen mevcut hastalıkları, ulaşımı engellemeyen hafif yağmurları ve iflas veya fiziksel devamsızlık içermeyen tedarikçi hatalarını geri ödeme kapsamı dışında bırakan sözleşmesel poliçe sınırlarıdır.

Poliçe istisnalarını dikkatlice okumak planlama sürecinde sürprizlerle karşılaşmanızı önler:

- **Fikir Değişikliği:** 2025 Insurance Information Institute raporuna (report) göre, çiftlerden biri veya her ikisi düğünü iptal etmeye karar verirse geleneksel poliçeler $0 öder (ancak bazı sigortacılar en az 12 ay önceden satın alınması halinde yalnızca masrafları ödeyen ebeveynleri koruyan özel bir kloz sunar).
- **Önceden Var Olan Tıbbi Durumlar:** Poliçe satın alınmadan önceki 60 ila 180 gün içinde bilinen veya tedavi edilen sağlık sorunlarından kaynaklanan iptaller kapsam dışıdır.
- **Resmi Uyarı Olmayan Hava Koşulları:** Açık hava fotoğraflarını zorlaştıran ancak yolları kapatmayan veya mekanı kullanılamaz hale getirmeyen hafif yağmur ya da kar iptal teminatını tetiklemez.

---

## Connecticut'taki Kutlamanız İçin Düğün Sigortasına Değer mi?

Düğün sigortası, 2025 Insurance Information Institute tüketici çalışmasına (study) göre bir çiftin iade edilmeyen tedarikçi depozitolarına $5,000'dan fazla yatırım yaptığı, konuklara alkol ikram ettiği veya Connecticut'ta mekan hasarlarından sorumlu tutan bir sözleşme imzaladığı her durumda satın alınmaya değer bir güvencedir.

Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I) tarafından yapılan 2025 maliyet-fayda çalışmasına (study report) göre, $350 ila $550 tutarındaki kapsamlı bir düğün poliçesi ortalama $42,000 olan Connecticut düğün bütçesinin yalnızca %1'ini temsil etmekte ve toplam depozito ile sorumluluk riskinde prim maliyetinin 100x katına kadar koruma sağlamaktadır.

---

## Doğrulanabilir Connecticut Düğün ve Etkinlik Sigortası Ölçütleri

Connecticut genelindeki çiftler, düğün organizatörleri ve risk danışmanları etkinlik teminatı seçerken doğrulanabilir sektör verilerine güvenir:

- The Knot 2025 Real Weddings Study raporuna (study report) göre, Connecticut ve New York üç eyalet bölgesinde ortalama düğün maliyeti $36,000 ila $48,000 arasında değişmekte olup çiftler ortalama 12 ila 14 ayrı tedarikçiyle sözleşme imzalamaktadır.
- Travelers Insurance ve Triple-I tarafından yayınlanan 2025 düğün sigortası hasar raporuna (report) göre, düğün hasar taleplerinin %41'i tedarikçi iflaslarından veya gelmemesinden, %21'i şiddetli hava ertelemelerinden ve %18'i ani hastalık veya yaralanmalardan kaynaklanmaktadır.
- National Association for Catering and Events (NACE) 2025 mekan sözleşmesi anket raporuna (survey report) göre, Connecticut'taki ticari düğün mekanlarının, tarihi malikanelerin ve bağ evlerinin %85'inden fazlası tesisi Ek Sigortalı olarak gösteren $1,000,000 limitli bir Sigorta Sertifikası (COI) zorunlu tutmaktadır.
- Connecticut Genel Yasaları Bölüm 30-102 hakkındaki 2025 yasal sorumluluk araştırma raporlarına (research reports) göre, alkolle ilgili yaralanma davaları $250,000'a kadar yasal Dram Shop tazminatını ve sınırsız genel hukuk ihmal davalarını tetikleyebilmektedir.

---

## Connecticut Mekan Sözleşmeleri ve Sorumluluk Üzerine Uzman Görüşü

> "Acente inceleme raporumuza (agency report) göre çoğu çift düğünlerinden otuz gün önce Danbury, Bridgeport veya Watertown ofislerimizi arıyor çünkü mekanları aniden mülkü Ek Sigortalı olarak gösteren $1,000,000 limitli bir Sigorta Sertifikası istiyor. Bu sorumluluk COI belgesini yaklaşık $175 karşılığında 24 saat içinde düzenleyebilsek de, iptal teminatınızı ilk mekan depozitonuzu yatırdığınız hafta satın almak $20,000 veya daha fazlasını tedarikçi iflaslarına ve fırtınalara karşı korur."
> — Ron T. Boucher, Principal Agent, Associated Insurance Agency (2026)

---

## Connecticut'ta Düğün Sigortası Hakkında Sıkça Sorulan Sorular (SSS)

### Connecticut'ta Düğün Sigortası Ne Kadar Tutar?

Connecticut düğün sigortası, 2025 Insurance Information Institute raporuna (report) göre tek başına $1,000,000 genel ve alkol sorumluluk poliçesi için $150 ila $275, veya $25,000 ila $50,000 iptal teminatıyla birleştirildiğinde $400 ila $850 tutan kısa vadeli bir etkinlik poliçesidir.

### Connecticut Düğün Mekanları Neden Sigorta Sertifikası (COI) Şart Koşar?

Düğün Sigorta Sertifikası, 2025 sektör anketine (survey) göre Connecticut davet salonlarının ve bağ evlerinin %85'inden fazlası tarafından zorunlu tutulan ve mekanı konuk yaralanmalarına veya mülk hasarına karşı $1,000,000 sorumluluk korumasıyla Ek Sigortalı olarak gösteren sözleşmesel bir belgedir.

### Ev Sahibi Alkol Sorumluluğu Nedir ve Connecticut Yasaları Düğün Sahiplerini Nasıl Etkiler?

Ev sahibi alkol sorumluluğu, alkollü bir düğün konuğunun trafik kazasına neden olması durumunda yasal savunma ve tazminat masraflarını ödeyen ve 2025 hukuk raporlarında (reports) incelenen Connecticut Genel Yasaları Bölüm 30-102 kapsamında düğün sahiplerini koruyan bir etkinlik sigortası teminatıdır.

### Düğün İptal Sigortası Tedarikçi İflasını veya Şiddetli Fırtınaları Karşılar mı?

Düğün iptal teminatı, 2025 Travelers düğün hasar çalışmasına (study) göre isimlendirilmiş bir fırtına, ani aile hastalığı veya tedarikçi iflasının ertelemeye zorlaması durumunda iade edilmeyen mekan, yemek ve fotoğrafçılık depozitolarını seçilen limite ($15,000 ila $100,000+) kadar geri ödeyen bir poliçedir.

---

## Düğün Sigorta Sertifikanızı ve Depozito Korumanızı Bugün Güvenceye Alın

Düğün bittikten sonra, nişan yüzüğünüzü ve alyanslarınızı muafiyetsiz kişisel eşya ek poliçesine kaydettirmeyi ve otomobil ile ev poliçelerinizi birleştirmeyi unutmayın — birlikte ilk evinizi satın alıyorsanız [tarihi Bridgeport ev alıcıları sigorta rehberimize](/tr/blog/historic-bridgeport-homebuyers-insurance-guide) göz atın.

Mekanınızın Sigorta Sertifikasını (COI) ve özel düğün iptal teklifinizi dakikalar içinde almak için bugün Danbury, Bridgeport veya Watertown'daki [Associated Insurance Agency](/tr/personal/homeowners) ile iletişime geçin.

        <div class="text-center space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-extrabold text-accent tracking-tight">
            Understanding Connecticut Certificates of Insurance
          </h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary max-w-2xl mx-auto">
            Clear guidelines on ACORD 25 requirements, additional insured language, and state statutory provisions.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-6">
          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              01
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is an ACORD 25 Certificate?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              The ACORD 25 is the nationally recognized standard form used by insurance brokers to certify policy existence. It summarizes policy numbers, carrier ratings, effective terms, and dollar limits for Commercial General Liability, Commercial Automobile, and Workers' Compensation.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              02
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Additional Insured Endorsements</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Commercial landlords, general contractors, and municipalities often require status as an Additional Insured (commonly forms CG 20 10 for ongoing operations and CG 20 37 for completed operations). An executed written contract is required prior to loss occurrence.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              03
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Waiver of Subrogation</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A Waiver of Subrogation endorsement prohibits the insurance carrier from pursuing financial recovery against the certificate holder after paying a loss. This protects the working relationship between subcontractors and project owners.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              04
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Primary & Non-Contributory</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              When contract specifications require "Primary and Non-Contributory" language, your policy will respond first to any covered claim, without seeking any contribution from the certificate holder's own commercial general liability policy.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Agency Support Contacts -->
        <div class="p-6 sm:p-8 rounded-2xl bg-zinc-950 text-white border border-zinc-800 space-y-6">
          <div class="flex flex-col sm:flex-row justify-between items-start sm:items-center gap-4 border-b border-zinc-800 pb-4">

            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Personal automobile policies explicitly exclude accidents occurring while carrying commercial cargo, transporting trade tools, charging for deliveries, or performing company errands. If an employee causes a severe crash during business hours, the personal carrier will typically deny coverage, exposing your business bank accounts to immediate civil liability.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            A dedicated commercial auto policy provides enterprise-grade liability limits, physical damage reimbursement, and legal defense costs specifically structured for business operations, fleet management, and commercial vehicle registrations in Connecticut.
          </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Does my personal auto insurance cover driving for business in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Almost universally, personal auto policies contain strict business-use exclusions. If you or an employee is involved in an accident while transporting tools, carrying commercial cargo, delivering goods, or traveling between client job sites, the personal insurer can deny the claim entirely, exposing your company to catastrophic personal liability.
            </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is Hired and Non-Owned Auto (HNOA) insurance?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Hired and Non-Owned Auto (HNOA) covers liability when your business rents or leases vehicles, or when employees drive their personal cars to run company errands (such as driving to the bank, picking up supplies, or meeting clients). If they cause an accident, HNOA protects your company against third-party lawsuits once the employee's personal policy limits are exhausted.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Does commercial auto insurance cover tools and cargo inside company trucks?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Standard commercial auto policies cover the physical vehicle and permanently attached fixtures (like tool racks or utility bodies), but they do NOT automatically cover loose tools, specialized equipment, or client cargo. To protect hand tools, diagnostic gear, and materials, AIA adds an Inland Marine / Tool and Equipment Floater endorsement.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What commercial liability limits should Connecticut businesses carry?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              While Connecticut minimum financial responsibility limits under CGS § 14-112 are only $25k/$50k/$25k, these are woefully inadequate for businesses. Commercial trucks and fleets typically carry at least a $500,000 to $1,000,000 Combined Single Limit (CSL), frequently paired with a Commercial Umbrella policy for broader asset protection.
            </p>
          </div>

            What Does Commercial General Liability Cover in Connecticut?
          </h2>

Policies cover medical payments, attorney fees, settlement negotiations, and court judgments.

CGL is the cornerstone of every Connecticut commercial risk plan.
          </p>

            Why General Contractors & Landlords Demand It
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            In Connecticut, virtually no commercial landlord will hand over the keys to a retail storefront or warehouse without proof of at least $1,000,000 in General Liability coverage naming them as an <strong>Additional Insured</strong>.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Similarly, general contractors (GCs) require all subcontractors—including electricians, framers, roofers, and HVAC technicians—to provide an active ACORD certificate before stepping foot on a job site.

          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Common questions from Connecticut business owners about General Liability.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Is General Liability insurance required by law in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              While Connecticut state statutes do not universally mandate general liability for every business entity, it is practically mandatory. Commercial landlords require it before signing leases, municipal agencies and general contractors demand proof of coverage (COI) before awarding contracts, and Connecticut licensing boards for trades (electricians, plumbers, home improvement contractors) require active liability policies.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">How quickly can Associated Insurance Agency issue a Certificate of Insurance (COI)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              For active policyholders, Associated Insurance Agency issues standard ACORD 25 Certificates of Insurance (COIs) same-day, often within minutes of receiving your request. This ensures contractors and vendors can bid on jobs, enter job sites, and satisfy client requirements without project delays.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What policy limits are standard for General Liability in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              The standard baseline for commercial general liability in Connecticut is $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate ($1M/$2M). High-risk contractors, commercial tenants, or businesses working on municipal projects often purchase Commercial Umbrella or Excess Liability policies to increase limits to $5,000,000 or $10,000,000.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is the difference between a standalone General Liability policy and a BOP?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

      <!-- CT Legal Mandate / Search Intent Snippet -->
      <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-10 items-start">
        <div class="lg:col-span-7 space-y-5">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent tracking-tight">
            Connecticut Workers' Compensation Laws (CGS § 31-284)
          </h2>
          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Under the Connecticut Workers' Compensation Act (CGS § 31-284), all employers regularly employing one or more workers must provide proof of solvent workers' compensation insurance. The policy covers statutory medical care, rehabilitation, and temporary or permanent wage replacement. In exchange, the law establishes an "exclusive remedy" doctrine granting employers immunity from civil personal injury lawsuits.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Operating without workers' compensation in Connecticut is a class D felony risk. The Workers' Compensation Commission and Department of Labor conduct active workplace investigations. Uninsured employers face mandatory stop-work orders and civil fines starting at $500 per day, plus personal liability for all injured worker medical costs.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
            <span class="w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-accent-gold"></span>
            Penalties for Non-Compliance in CT
          </h3>
          <div class="space-y-3 text-xs text-text-secondary">
            <div class="p-3 bg-red-50 text-red-900 rounded border border-red-200">
              <strong>Mandatory Stop-Work Orders:</strong> The state can shut down all job sites and business premises until compliant coverage is verified.
            </div>
            <div class="p-3 bg-zinc-50 rounded border border-border-subtle">
              <strong>$500 Daily Fines:</strong> Fines accumulate daily for every calendar day an employer operated without active coverage.
            </div>
            <div class="p-3 bg-zinc-50 rounded border border-border-subtle">
              <strong>Unlimited Civil Liability:</strong> If an employee is injured without insurance, the exclusive remedy defense is nullified, opening personal bank accounts to civil litigation.
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Two Core Parts of a Policy -->
      <div class="space-y-8">
        <div class="text-center max-w-2xl mx-auto space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">How Workers' Compensation Protects Both Parties</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">A standard policy consists of two distinct statutory parts.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-8">
          <div class="bg-white p-8 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
            <div class="w-12 h-12 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-base">Part 1</div>
            <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-text-primary">Workers' Compensation (Statutory Benefits)</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Provides direct benefits mandated by Connecticut law to employees injured on the job, regardless of fault:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs text-text-secondary pt-2">
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Medical Care:</strong> 100% of hospital, doctor, surgical, prescription, and physical therapy expenses.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Wage Replacement:</strong> Temporary Total (TT) or Temporary Partial (TP) disability benefits equal to 75% of spendable weekly wage.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Vocational Rehab:</strong> Retraining benefits if the employee cannot return to their previous trade.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Death Benefits:</strong> Funeral expense stipends and financial support for surviving dependents.
              </li>
            </ul>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-8 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
            <div class="w-12 h-12 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-base">Part 2</div>
            <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-text-primary">Employers' Liability (Civil Defense Shield)</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Shields the employer against third-party lawsuits and civil damages that fall outside statutory workers' compensation:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs text-text-secondary pt-2">
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Third-Party Action Over:</strong> Protects when an injured employee sues a general contractor or property owner who in turn sues you.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Dual Capacity Lawsuits:</strong> Defends against claims that you injured an employee in a role other than direct employer.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Loss of Consortium:</strong> Covers civil claims brought by an injured employee’s spouse or family members.
              </li>
              <li class="flex items-center gap-2">
                <span class="text-accent-gold font-bold">✓</span> <strong>Legal Defense:</strong> Pays attorney retainers, depositions, and litigation defense fees.
              </li>
            </ul>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Audits & Payroll Optimization -->

        <div class="text-center space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Answers to critical questions regarding Connecticut Workers' Compensation.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Is Workers' Compensation mandatory for small businesses in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Under the Connecticut Workers' Compensation Act (CGS § 31-284), any business that employs one or more individuals—regardless of whether they are full-time, part-time, seasonal, or family members—must maintain active workers' compensation insurance. Failure to do so can result in state-issued stop-work orders and civil fines starting at $500 per day.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Can business owners or LLC members exclude themselves from Workers' Comp coverage?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Sole proprietors, single-member LLCs, and corporate officers in Connecticut have the legal option to exclude themselves from coverage using state Form 6B or Form 75 to reduce premium costs. However, if they hire even one part-time assistant or apprentice, they must purchase a policy covering that employee.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is a 'Ghost Policy' in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A 'Ghost Policy' (or minimum premium policy) is an affordable workers' compensation policy purchased by a self-employed sole proprietor or independent contractor with zero employees. It provides a valid Certificate of Insurance (COI) to satisfy general contractor or client contract mandates without paying for unnecessary payroll coverage.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">How does the annual Workers' Compensation payroll audit work?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              At policy expiration, your insurance carrier compares your estimated payroll against your actual state wage filings (Forms CT-941 and W-2/1099s). If your payroll was higher or if subcontractors lacked certificates, you receive an adjustment bill. Associated Insurance Agency works with you throughout the policy term to adjust payroll declarations and verify classification codes so you avoid unexpected audit bills.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

              Contratistas generales y municipios exigen figurar como Asegurado Adicional (formularios CG 20 10 y CG 20 37) para protegerse contra responsabilidades derivadas de sus trabajos. Se requiere contrato escrito previo.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              03
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Renuncia de Subrogación</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Prohíbe a la compañía de seguros reclamar legalmente el reembolso al titular del certificado tras indemnizar un siniestro, protegiendo las relaciones comerciales entre subcontratistas y clientes.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              04
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Primario y No Contributorio</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Cuando el contrato exige redacción "Primaria y No Contributoria", su póliza responderá en primer lugar ante cualquier reclamo cubierto, sin solicitar aporte a la póliza del cliente.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

En caso de accidente grave, la aseguradora personal rechazará el reclamo, dejando a su empresa expuesta a demandas multimillonarias.

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Qué es el seguro de Auto Alquilado y No Propio (HNOA)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La cobertura HNOA protege a su empresa cuando sus empleados utilizan sus propios autos personales para realizar tareas de la compañía (ir al banco, buscar materiales o visitar clientes) o cuando alquila vehículos temporalmente. Si causan un accidente, esta cobertura protege su empresa una vez agotados los límites del empleado.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Las pólizas comerciales estándar cubren el vehículo físico y los accesorios fijos, pero no las herramientas sueltas o maquinaria transportada. Para proteger herramientas manuales, generadores o materiales, AIA incluye un endoso de 'Inland Marine' o seguro de equipo móvil.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Aunque los mínimos estatales de Connecticut (CGS § 14-112) son de solo $25k/$50k/$25k, son insuficientes para empresas. La mayoría de los vehículos de trabajo y flotas aseguran límites combinados (CSL) de $500,000 a $1,000,000, frecuentemente complementados con un Paraguas Comercial.
            </p>

            En Connecticut, prácticamente ningún dueño de local comercial entregará las llaves sin una prueba de al menos $1,000,000 en Responsabilidad General nombrándolo como <strong>Asegurado Adicional</strong>.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Asimismo, los contratistas generales exigen a carpinteros, plomeros, electricistas y techadores un certificado ACORD vigente antes de permitirles el ingreso a la obra.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Lesiones Corporales a Terceros</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Cubre costos de hospital, traslados en ambulancia y compensaciones si un cliente, visitante o repartidor se lesiona dentro de sus instalaciones.

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Es obligatorio por ley el seguro de Responsabilidad Civil General en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Aunque los estatutos de Connecticut no exigen universalmente la responsabilidad civil general para todas las empresas, es prácticamente indispensable. Los arrendadores comerciales la exigen para firmar contratos de alquiler, las agencias municipales y contratistas generales solicitan pruebas de cobertura (COI) antes de otorgar obras, y las juntas de licencias de oficios exigen pólizas vigentes.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Con qué rapidez puede Associated Insurance Agency emitir un Certificado de Seguro (COI)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Para asegurados activos, Associated Insurance Agency emite Certificados de Seguro estándar ACORD 25 el mismo día, frecuentemente en cuestión de minutos. Esto permite a los contratistas licitar trabajos, ingresar a sitios de construcción y cumplir con los requisitos del cliente sin retrasos.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuáles son los límites de póliza habituales en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El estándar de referencia para responsabilidad general comercial en Connecticut es de $1,000,000 por incidente y $2,000,000 acumulado general ($1M/$2M). Contratistas de mayor riesgo o empresas que realizan obras públicas suelen adquirir pólizas Paraguas Comercial para elevar los límites a $5,000,000 o más.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre una póliza de Responsabilidad General independiente y una BOP?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Una póliza independiente solo cubre reclamos de terceros por lesiones y daños materiales. Una Póliza para Propietarios de Negocios (BOP) combina la Responsabilidad General con el Seguro de Propiedad Comercial y la Pérdida de Ingresos en un solo paquete con tarifa reducida, ideal para pequeños comercios y oficinas.
            </p>
          </div>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Es obligatorio el seguro de compensación laboral en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Según la Ley de Compensación de Trabajadores de Connecticut (CGS § 31-284), cualquier empresa con uno o más empleados (ya sean de tiempo completo, medio tiempo o estacionales) debe contar con seguro de compensación de trabajadores. No cumplir con la ley conlleva órdenes de paralización inmediata y multas estatales de al menos $500 por día.

Sin embargo, en el momento en que contratan a un trabajador adicional, deben contar con una póliza activa para dicho empleado.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

En AIA le ayudamos a clasificar adecuadamente a su personal para evitar cobros sorpresa al final del año.

            Requisitos de Seguro de Auto en Connecticut (CGS § 14-112)

          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              La ley de Connecticut exige límites mínimos de responsabilidad civil: $25,000 por lesiones por persona, $50,000 por accidente y $25,000 por daños a la propiedad (25/50/25), además de cobertura equivalente para conductores sin seguro (UM/UIM).
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Cumplir con el mínimo legal permite registrar el vehículo en el DMV, pero $25,000 por daños materiales no alcanza para reponer la mayoría de los vehículos en Connecticut hoy en día. Si causa un choque con varios heridos o destruye un auto reciente, las cuentas médicas y de taller superan el mínimo estatal con rapidez. Cualquier saldo que exceda su póliza saldrá de su propio bolsillo.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">
            Por qué el mínimo de 25/50/25 arriesga su patrimonio
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            El precio promedio de un auto nuevo supera los $48,000. Si su límite de daños a la propiedad es de $25,000, usted responde personalmente por la diferencia.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Cuando la póliza se agota, los tribunales de Connecticut pueden autorizar embargos sobre sus cuentas bancarias, el valor de su vivienda o retener ingresos futuros. Subir su cobertura a 100/300/100 o 250/500/100 representa una diferencia mínima al mes y protege sus bienes.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Detalle de protecciones obligatorias de responsabilidad y coberturas de daños al vehículo.</p>

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Responsabilidad por Daños a la Propiedad</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Cubre reparaciones de otros vehículos, barandillas, postes o estructuras dañadas en un accidente donde usted sea responsable.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">03</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Cobertura de Colisión</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Paga la reparación o reemplazo de su propio vehículo si choca contra otro auto, patina sobre hielo contra una barrera o vuelca, menos su deducible.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">04</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Cobertura Integral</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuáles son los límites mínimos obligatorios de seguro de auto en Connecticut (CGS § 14-112)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Bajo la ley de Connecticut (CGS § 14-112), todo conductor debe portar una cobertura mínima de responsabilidad civil de $25,000 por lesiones por persona, $50,000 por accidente en total y $25,000 por daños a la propiedad (25/50/25), además de cobertura equivalente para conductores sin seguro o con seguro insuficiente (UM/UIM).
            </p>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El precio promedio de un auto nuevo supera los $48,000. Si causa un choque que destruye un auto reciente, el límite estatal de $25,000 deja una diferencia de más de $20,000 que saldrá de su propio bolsillo. Si los gastos médicos de los lesionados superan los $50,000 de su póliza, pueden demandar sus cuentas de ahorro y su vivienda. Recomendamos contratar límites de al menos 100/300/100 o 250/500/100.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre cobertura de Colisión e Integral en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La cobertura de Colisión paga la reparación o reemplazo de su propio auto si choca contra otro vehículo, un poste o patina en hielo. La cobertura Integral cubre daños ajenos a una colisión: impacto con venados en carreteras rurales, piedras en el parabrisas, robo, vandalismo, incendio y ramas caídas por tormentas.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Puedo asegurar una casa rodante, cámper o remolque en la misma póliza?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La mayoría de las aseguradoras requieren una póliza especializada para vehículos recreativos en vez de añadirlos a una póliza de auto estándar. Podemos emitir ambas pólizas con la misma compañía para aprovechar descuentos y cubrir responsabilidad en campamentos, remolque y pertenencias personales.
            </p>

También incluye cobertura de responsabilidad civil si un invitado se lesiona en su propiedad.

Associated Insurance Agency trabaja con aseguradoras como Travelers, Safeco, Hanover y Liberty Mutual para ajustar la cobertura al costo real de reconstrucción de su vivienda.

          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Muchos propietarios calculan su póliza según el precio de compra o el avalúo municipal. Lo que realmente cuenta es el costo de reconstrucción: el valor de los materiales y la mano de obra local necesarios para reconstruir desde cero.
          </p>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre el costo de reemplazo y el valor de mercado?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El valor de mercado es lo que un comprador paga por su casa, incluyendo el terreno y el vecindario. El costo de reconstrucción es el costo de materiales y mano de obra necesario para rehacer la vivienda desde cero. En Connecticut, los costos de construcción y mano de obra están entre los más altos del país, por lo que el costo de reconstrucción suele ser muy diferente del valor de tasación inmobiliaria.
            </p>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cubre el seguro de hogar de Connecticut los daños por congelación de tuberías y acumulación de hielo?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Sí. Las pólizas estándar HO-3 y HO-5 generalmente cubren tuberías rotas por frío y filtraciones por presas de hielo en el techo, siempre que se haya mantenido la calefacción en la vivienda. Sin embargo, los daños por agua de alcantarillado o drenajes requieren un endoso adicional.
            </p>

Cuando una demanda agota los límites de su póliza primaria, la sombrilla cubre el saldo restante hasta el límite contratado ($1,000,000 a $5,000,000 o más).

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Las demandas judiciales no afectan únicamente a familias adineradas. Los factores de riesgo más habituales incluyen conductores jóvenes, piscinas, perros y propiedades en alquiler.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

              <svg class="w-5 h-5" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M11.48 3.499c.3-.921 1.603-.921 1.902 0l1.519 4.674a1 1 0 0 0 .95.69h4.915c.969 0 1.371 1.24.588 1.81l-3.976 2.888a1 1 0 0 0-.363 1.118l1.518 4.674c.3.922-.755 1.688-1.538 1.118l-3.976-2.888a1 1 0 0 0-1.176 0l-3.976 2.888c-.783.57-1.838-.197-1.538-1.118l1.518-4.674a1 1 0 0 0-.363-1.118l-3.976-2.888c-.784-.57-.38-1.81.588-1.81h4.914a1 1 0 0 0 .951-.69l1.519-4.674Z" />
              </svg>
            </div>
            <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-accent">¿Qué protege el seguro para inquilinos y líneas especializadas en Connecticut?</h2>
            <div class="p-3.5 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
                Mientras la póliza del propietario solo cubre la estructura física del edificio, el seguro para inquilinos protege sus pertenencias personales (computadoras, ropa, muebles) contra robo, incendios y daños, incluyendo responsabilidad personal. AIA también gestiona pólizas especializadas para vehículos recreativos (lanchas, casas rodantes) y seguro veterinario para mascotas en Connecticut.
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              También emitimos pólizas para inquilinos y líneas personales especializadas. El seguro de su arrendador solo cubre la estructura del edificio; no cubre sus pertenencias personales, muebles ni lesiones de invitados dentro de su apartamento.
            </p>
            <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 pt-1">
              <a href="/es/quote?type=renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-gold hover:text-accent-gold-hover transition-colors">
                Solicitar Cotización de Inquilinos
                <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                  <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M13.5 4.5 21 12m0 0-7.5 7.5M21 12H3" />
                </svg>
              </a>
              <a href="/es/personal/renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent hover:underline">
                Explorar Guía de Inquilinos y Preguntas Frecuentes →
              </a>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="lg:col-span-8 bg-bg-secondary p-8 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle space-y-6">
            <div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-6 text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Seguro de Inquilinos</h4>
                <p>Cubre el reemplazo de ropa, computadoras y muebles en caso de robo o incendio. Incluye responsabilidad civil del inquilino en caso de accidentes menores dentro de la unidad alquilada.</p>
              </div>
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Seguro para Mascotas</h4>
                <p>Planes de accidentes y enfermedades para perros y gatos. Cubre visitas veterinarias, cirugías y recetas médicas para que nunca tenga que tomar decisiones de salud basadas en el costo.</p>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

    </div>

            <h2 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Nuestro Compromiso con su Privacidad</h2>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <strong>Associated Insurance Agency</strong> ("AIA", "nosotros" o "nuestro") valora su confianza. Como agencia de seguros independiente que opera en Danbury, Watertown y Bridgeport, Connecticut, gestionamos información personal y financiera necesaria para obtener cotizaciones, emitir coberturas y administrar pólizas. Nunca vendemos sus datos personales ni números móviles a comercializadores externos o listas de telemercadeo.
            </p>

          <!-- Sección 1 -->
          <article id="vision-general" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 1</span>
              Visión General y Aviso de la Ley Gramm-Leach-Bliley (GLBA)
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Esta Política de Privacidad describe cómo Associated Insurance Agency recopila, utiliza, resguarda y divulga información personal e información financiera personal no pública (NPI) a través de nuestro sitio web (<a href="https://aia-danbury.com/es" class="text-accent underline font-medium">https://aia-danbury.com/es</a>), cotizadores en línea, llamadas telefónicas y consultas presenciales.
            </p>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Conforme al Título V de la Ley Gramm-Leach-Bliley (GLBA) y las regulaciones del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut, las instituciones financieras y agencias de seguros autorizadas están obligadas a informar sus políticas y prácticas de privacidad a los consumidores.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 2 -->
          <article id="informacion-recopilada" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 2</span>
              Información que Recopilamos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Para evaluar el riesgo de seguro y solicitar propuestas precisas a las compañías aseguradoras, recopilamos las siguientes categorías de datos:
            </p>
            <div class="space-y-2.5 text-xs text-text-secondary">
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos de Contacto</strong>
                Nombre completo, dirección residencial y postal, correo electrónico, números telefónicos y oficina de preferencia.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos de Seguros y Suscripción</strong>
                Número de identificación del vehículo (VIN), historial de conducción, antigüedad y características de la propiedad, acreedores hipotecarios, aseguradora anterior y registros de reclamos.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Información Comercial</strong>
                Nombre comercial, identificación fiscal patronal (FEIN), nómina, ventas brutas, ubicaciones operativas y clasificaciones de negocio.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos Técnicos y de Seguridad</strong>
                Direcciones IP, navegador, sistema operativo, fecha/hora y parámetros de seguridad honeypot para mitigar envíos de bots automatizados.
              </div>
            </div>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 3: Confidencialidad Móvil Estricta (10DLC / CTIA) -->
          <article id="privacidad-movil" class="space-y-4 scroll-mt-28 p-6 bg-accent/5 border border-accent/20 rounded-xl">
            <div class="flex items-start gap-3">

              </svg>
              <div>
                <h2 class="text-lg font-bold text-accent">
                  Sección 3: Confidencialidad Estricta de Telefonía Móvil y Mensajes SMS (10DLC / CTIA)
                </h2>
                <div class="mt-2 p-3 bg-white border border-border-subtle rounded-lg text-sm text-text-primary font-medium leading-relaxed">
                  "No se compartirá información móvil con terceros o afiliados con fines de marketing o promocionales. Todas las demás categorías excluyen los datos de suscripción y consentimiento del originador de mensajes de texto; esta información no se compartirá con ningún tercero."
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              En nuestros formularios en línea, nuestro aviso indica: <em>"Proporcionar un número permite llamadas/mensajes de texto de nuestra parte sobre el mensaje."</em>
            </p>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Su número de teléfono celular y el consentimiento para SMS son utilizados <strong>exclusivamente</strong> por Associated Insurance Agency para comunicarse directamente con usted con relación a su solicitud de cotización, servicio de póliza o renovaciones. Jamás vendemos, alquilamos ni cedemos su número ni el consentimiento de suscripción a terceros o redes de comercialización.
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-1 text-xs text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li>Puede cancelar las comunicaciones por SMS en cualquier momento respondiendo <strong>STOP</strong>.</li>
              <li>Responda <strong>HELP</strong> para obtener asistencia o información de servicio al cliente.</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 4 -->
          <article id="uso-informacion" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 4</span>
              Cómo Usamos su Información
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Utilizamos los datos recopilados estrictamente para operaciones legítimas de correduría de seguros:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li><strong>Comparación de Tarifas:</strong> Enviar los datos preliminares a aseguradoras líderes autorizadas para comparar precios y pólizas.</li>
              <li><strong>Servicio de Pólizas:</strong> Asistir en la adición de vehículos o conductores, expedición de certificados (COI) y consultas de facturación.</li>
              <li><strong>Comunicación Directa:</strong> Contactarlo por teléfono, correo electrónico, mensaje de texto o correo postal sobre sus cotizaciones o pólizas activas.</li>
              <li><strong>Prevención de Fraudes:</strong> Proteger nuestros sistemas contra envíos automatizados no deseados y solicitudes maliciosas.</li>
              <li><strong>Cumplimiento Legal:</strong> Cumplir con las normativas y requerimientos del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut.</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 5 -->
          <article id="divulgacion-aseguradoras" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 5</span>
              Divulgación y Compartición de Información
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Como agencia independiente, AIA comparte sus datos únicamente con las partes necesarias para procesar sus trámites de seguros:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li><strong>Compañías Aseguradoras:</strong> Para cotizar, evaluar el riesgo y emitir pólizas (Safeco, Travelers, Progressive, The Hartford, Foremost, Guard, etc.).</li>
              <li><strong>Agencias de Informes del Consumidor:</strong> Las aseguradoras pueden solicitar reportes de manejo (MVR) e historial de reclamos (C.L.U.E.).</li>
              <li><strong>Proveedores de Tecnología:</strong> Empresas que alojan nuestros sistemas de gestión de pólizas bajo estrictos acuerdos de confidencialidad.</li>
              <li><strong>Autoridades Gubernamentales:</strong> En respuesta a órdenes judiciales o requerimientos del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut.</li>
            </ul>
            <p class="text-xs font-semibold text-accent pt-1">
              NO VENDEMOS NI ALQUILAMOS SU INFORMACIÓN PERSONAL A TERCEROS PARA PUBLICIDAD COMERCIAL.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 6 -->
          <article id="cookies-registros" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 6</span>
              Cookies y Registros Técnicos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Nuestro sitio web utiliza cookies de sesión estándar y mecanismos de seguridad para garantizar una navegación fluida y evitar formularios falsos. No utilizamos píxeles invasivos ni rastreadores de perfiles de terceros con fines publicitarios.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 7 -->
          <article id="seguridad-datos" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 7</span>
              Medidas de Seguridad y Protección de Datos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              AIA implementa medidas de seguridad físicas, electrónicas y de procedimiento de conformidad con los estándares de la ley GLBA y la Ley de Privacidad de Datos de Connecticut (CTDPA). Esto incluye cifrado SSL/TLS, cortafuegos y acceso restringido exclusivo para agentes autorizados.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 8 -->
          <article id="retencion-datos" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 8</span>
              Requisitos de Retención de Documentos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Las agencias de seguros están sujetas a normas estatales y federales de conservación de registros. Conservamos expedientes de asegurados, solicitudes y comunicaciones durante los períodos exigidos por la ley estatal (generalmente entre 5 y 7 años tras el vencimiento o cancelación de la póliza).
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 9 -->
          <article id="derechos-usuario" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">

              Sus Derechos de Privacidad
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Conforme a la legislación aplicable y sujeto a los requisitos de archivo regulatorio, usted tiene derecho a:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-1.5 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li>Solicitar acceso para revisar los datos personales en su expediente activo.</li>
              <li>Solicitar la corrección de datos incorrectos o desactualizados.</li>
              <li>Darse de baja de comunicaciones comerciales (respondiendo STOP o mediante enlaces de correo).</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 10 -->
          <article id="privacidad-menores" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 10</span>
              Privacidad de Menores (COPPA)
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Este sitio está destinado a adultos y propietarios de empresas. No recopilamos conscientemente información de menores de 13 años. Si cree que un menor nos ha provisto datos, comuníquese con nosotros para eliminarlos inmediatamente.
            </p>
          </article>

          <article id="modificaciones" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">

              Modificaciones a esta Política
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              AIA se reserva el derecho de actualizar esta Política de Privacidad periódicamente. Toda modificación entrará en vigor al publicarse con la fecha de actualización correspondiente.

              Contacto con el Responsable de Privacidad

            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Como agencia independiente, AIA representa a múltiples compañías aseguradoras terceras (incluyendo Safeco, Travelers, Progressive, The Hartford, Foremost, entre otras).
            </p>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

La cobertura solo entra en vigencia una vez que un agente de seguros con licencia autorizado haya confirmado directamente por escrito su emisión o modificación, y el pago inicial obligatorio haya sido procesado por la compañía aseguradora correspondiente.

En caso de discrepancia, prevalecerá el contrato de póliza emitido por la compañía aseguradora.

        <div class="lg:col-span-7 space-y-5">

            Connecticut Auto Insurance Mandates (CGS § 14-112)
          </h2>
          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Connecticut law requires every motor vehicle owner to maintain financial responsibility with minimum liability limits of $25,000 bodily injury per person, $50,000 per accident, and $25,000 property damage (25/50/25), plus matching Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) protection.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Meeting that minimum lets you legally register a car with the DMV, but $25,000 in property damage does not even cover the replacement cost of an average vehicle on Connecticut roads today. If you cause an accident with multiple injuries or total a newer car, repair and medical bills exceed state minimums fast. Any balance beyond your policy limits comes out of your own pocket.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">
            Why 25/50/25 Limits Put Your Assets at Risk
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            The average new car sold today costs over $48,000. If your property damage cap is $25,000, you are personally liable for the rest.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            If damages exceed your policy, the other driver's attorney can pursue your personal bank accounts, place liens on your home, or garnish future wages under Connecticut court judgments. Stepping up to 100/300/100 or 250/500/100 liability usually adds only a modest amount to your monthly bill while protecting your assets.
          </p>

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

              Pays for damage from hazards other than crashes: hitting a deer on a rural backroad, stone chips on the windshield, theft, vandalism, storm flooding, and fallen tree branches.
            </p>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What are Connecticut's mandatory auto insurance minimums (CGS § 14-112)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Under Connecticut General Statutes (CGS § 14-112), registered drivers must carry liability coverage of at least $25,000 bodily injury per person, $50,000 total bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 property damage (25/50/25), along with matching Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) coverage.

If you cause a crash that totals a late-model car, a $25,000 property damage cap leaves a $23,000 gap that you have to pay out of pocket. If medical expenses for other passengers exceed your $50,000 bodily injury limit, injured parties can seek judgments against your personal savings and real estate. We recommend carrying at least 100/300/100 or 250/500/100 in liability.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Comprehensive covers damage from incidents outside a crash: hitting a deer or wild animal, windshield chips and cracks, theft, vandalism, fire, and branches knocked down during storms.

      <!-- What is Homeowners / Answer Framing Snippet -->
      <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-10 items-start">
        <div class="lg:col-span-7 space-y-5">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent tracking-tight">
            What Does Homeowners Insurance Cover in Connecticut?
          </h2>
          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Connecticut homeowners insurance pays to repair or rebuild your home and replace personal belongings after damage from fire, lightning, wind, hail, heavy snow, or vandalism. It also includes liability coverage if a guest is injured on your property.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Homes in Western Connecticut range from older houses in Litchfield County to coastal properties in Fairfield County, each with different rebuilding costs and storm risks. Associated Insurance Agency works with carriers including Travelers, Safeco, Hanover, and Liberty Mutual to match coverage to your home's actual rebuild value.
          </p>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
            <span class="w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-accent-gold"></span>
            Replacement Cost vs. Market Value
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Many homeowners base their coverage on purchase price or town tax assessments. What matters instead is dwelling replacement cost: the actual price of materials and local contractor labor needed to rebuild from scratch.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            We calculate coverage using regional rebuilding cost indexes and offer extended replacement cost endorsements (up to 125% to 150%) so sharp spikes in material costs do not leave you short after a major claim.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Core Coverage Grid -->
      <div class="space-y-8">
        <div class="text-center max-w-2xl mx-auto space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Standard Policy Coverage (HO-3 & HO-5)</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">How HO-3 and HO-5 policies break down essential protections.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">A</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage A: Dwelling</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to repair or rebuild your home's physical structure, including the foundation, roof, walls, and built-in appliances, after fire, wind, or storm damage.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">B</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage B: Other Structures</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers detached structures on your property, including garages, sheds, fences, driveways, and pools.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">C</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage C: Personal Property</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to replace furniture, clothing, electronics, and household goods if they are damaged, destroyed, or stolen at home or while traveling.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">D</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage D: Loss of Use</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays temporary living costs (such as hotel stays, short-term rentals, meals, and storage) if covered damage makes your home unlivable during repairs.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">E</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage E: Personal Liability</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers legal defense costs and settlements if a guest is injured on your property or you accidentally damage someone else's property.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">F</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage F: Medical Payments</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers medical bills for guests injured on your property, regardless of fault, helping handle minor accidents without legal claims.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

            <p class="text-text-muted">Covers sudden mechanical or electrical failure of heating systems, AC compressors, heat pumps, and electrical panels.</p>

          <div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">

            <p class="text-text-muted">Provides agreed-value, zero-deductible coverage for jewelry, watches, art, and collections that exceed standard policy limits.</p>
          </div>

        <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Answers to common Connecticut home insurance inquiries.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is the difference between dwelling replacement cost and market value?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Market value is what a buyer pays for your home, including the land and neighborhood. Dwelling replacement cost is the labor and material cost required to rebuild the house from the ground up. Connecticut has some of the highest construction and labor rates in the country, so rebuild costs often differ substantially from real estate market value or property tax assessments.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Does standard Connecticut homeowners insurance cover winter freeze damage and ice dams?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Standard HO-3 and HO-5 policies generally cover burst pipes and water damage from roof ice dams, as long as you maintained heat in the home. However, damage from backed-up sewer or drainage lines requires a separate water backup endorsement.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Is flood damage covered under a standard homeowners policy?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              No. Homeowners policies exclude flood damage from rising surface water, overflowing rivers, and coastal storm surges. Flood coverage requires a separate policy through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or private flood carriers, which Associated Insurance Agency can bind on your behalf.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">How much can I save by bundling home and auto insurance in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Bundling your home and auto policies with the same insurance carrier usually lowers both premiums by 15% to 25%, puts your coverage on a single billing account, and makes claims easier to coordinate.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
